translation: —"You misunderstood me," she said. "I did not come to quarrel with you, though I do not love you. I... I came to you... to speak like a human. Having summoned you, I already decided what I would say to you, and I will not budge from my decision, even if you do not understand me at all. It will be worse for you, not for me. I wanted to reply to what you wrote me, and to do it personally because it seemed more convenient to me. Listen to my reply to all your letters: for the first time I felt sorry for Prince Lev Nikolayevich the very day I met him, and when I learned all that happened at your evening. I felt sorry for him because he is such a simple person and believed in his simplicity that he could be happy... with a woman... of that sort. What I feared for him has come true: you could not love him, you tormented him and left him. You could not love him because you are too proud... no, not proud, I was mistaken, you are too vain... not even that: you are so self-centered that it borders on madness, as your letters to me prove. You could not love such a simple man, and maybe even despised and laughed at him privately. You could love only your own disgrace and the unceasing thought that you were disgraced and insulted. Had you had less disgrace or none at all, you would have been unhappier... (Aglaya relished saying these words, which had sprung too hastily, but were already prepared and well thought out, even at that moment when in a dream she could not have imagined this meeting; she watched with a venomous look the effect of her words on the agitated face of Nastasya Filipovna). Do you remember, she continued, "when he wrote me a letter; he says that you knew about this letter and even read it? From this letter I understood everything, and correctly understood it; he himself confirmed this to me recently, that is, word for word, everything I am saying to you now. After the letter, I started to wait. I guessed that you had to come here, because you cannot be away from St. Petersburg: you are still too young and attractive for the provinces... Anyway, that is not my saying," she added, turning crimson and, from that moment on, the color did not leave her face until the end of her speech. —When I saw Prince Lev again, I was terribly sorry and hurt for him. Don't laugh; if you laugh, you are not worthy of understanding this...
source_text: — Вы не так поняли, — сказала она, — я с вами не пришла... ссориться, хотя я вас не люблю. Я... я пришла к вам... с человеческою речью. Призывая вас, я уже решила, о чем буду вам говорить, и от решения не отступлюсь, хотя бы вы и совсем меня не поняли. Тем для вас будет хуже, а не для меня. Я хотела вам ответить на то, что вы мне писали, и ответить лично, потому что мне это казалось удобнее. Выслушайте же мой ответ на все ваши письма: мне стало жаль князя Льва Николаевича в первый раз в тот самый день, когда я с ним познакомилась и когда потом узнала обо всем, что произошло на вашем вечере. Мне потому его стало жаль, что он такой простодушный человек и по простоте своей поверил, что может быть счастлив... с женщиной... такого характера. Чего я боялась за него, то и случилось: вы не могли его полюбить, измучили его и кинули. Вы потому его не могли любить, что слишком горды... нет, не горды, я ошиблась, а потому, что вы тщеславны... даже и не это: вы себялюбивы до... сумасшествия, чему доказательством служат и ваши письма ко мне. Вы его, такого простого, не могли полюбить, и даже, может быть, про себя презирали и смеялись над ним, могли полюбить только один свой позор и беспрерывную мысль о том, что вы опозорены и что вас оскорбили. Будь у вас меньше позору или не будь его вовсе, вы были бы несчастнее... (Аглая с наслаждением выговаривала эти слишком уж поспешно выскакивавшие, но давно уже приготовленные и обдуманные слова, тогда еще обдуманные, когда и во сне не представлялось теперешнего свидания; она ядовитым взглядом следила за эффектом их на искаженном от волнения лице Настасьи Филипповны). Вы помните, — продолжала она, — тогда он написал мне письмо; он говорит, что вы про это письмо знаете и даже читали его? По этому письму я всё поняла, и верно поняла; он недавно мне подтвердил это сам, то есть всё, что я теперь вам говорю, слово в слово даже. После письма я стала ждать. Я угадала, что вы должны приехать сюда, потому что вам нельзя же быть без Петербурга: вы еще слишком молоды и хороши собой для провинции... Впрочем, это тоже не мои слова, — прибавила она, ужасно покраснев, и с этой минуты краска уже не сходила с ее лица, вплоть до самого окончания речи. — Когда я увидала опять князя, мне стало ужасно за него больно и обидно. Не смейтесь; если вы будете смеяться, то вы недостойны это понять...

Calling you, I have already decided what I will tell you about, and I will not back down from my decision, even if you do not understand me at all. That will be worse for you, not for me. I wanted to answer you what you wrote to me, and answer personally, because it seemed to me more convenient. Listen to my answer to all your letters: I felt sorry for Prince Lev Nikolaevich for the first time on the very day when I met him and when I later learned about everything that happened at your evening. That's why I felt sorry for him because he was such a simple-hearted person and because of his simplicity he believed that he could be happy ... with a woman ... of such a character. What I was afraid for him, then happened: you could not love him, you tortured him and threw him away. You could not love him because you were too proud... no, not proud, I was mistaken, but because you are vain... not even that: you are selfish to the point of... madness, which your letters to to me. You could not love him, so simple, and perhaps even despised and laughed at him inwardly, could love only your own disgrace and the incessant thought that you were disgraced and insulted. If you had less disgrace or if you didn’t have it at all, you would be more unhappy ... (Aglaya uttered with pleasure these words that jumped out too hastily, but had long been prepared and considered, then still considered, when the present meeting was not even imagined in a dream; she followed with a venomous glance the effect they had on Nastasya Filippovna's face, contorted with excitement.) Do you remember,” she continued, “then he wrote me a letter; he says that you know about this letter and even read it? From this letter, I understood everything, and correctly understood; he recently confirmed this to me himself, that is, everything that I am now telling you, even word for word. After the letter, I began to wait. I guessed that you must come here, because you cannot be without Petersburg: you are still too young and good-looking for the provinces ... However, these are not my words either, ”she added, blushing terribly, and from that moment blushed never left her face until the very end of her speech. “When I saw the prince again, I felt terribly hurt and offended for him. Do not laugh; if you laugh, then you are not worthy to understand it ...

human_translations.translator_1: “You misunderstood me,” she said. “I did not come… to quarrel with you, however much I dislike you. I… I came to hold a reasonable, sensible discussion with you. In calling upon you, I had already decided what I was going to say to you, and shall not deviate from my resolution even if you failed to understand me totally. It will be so much the worse for you, and not for me. I wanted to reply to what you wrote to me, and I wanted to reply in person, because it seemed to me to be the most appropriate thing to do. Please hear my reply to all your letters. I felt sorry for Prince Lev Nikolayevich the first time I got to know him and later when I found out what had happened at your soirée. I felt sorry for him because he is such a simple-hearted man, and in his simplicity had supposed he could be happy… with a woman… with such a character. What I feared would happen to him has happened. You could not fall in love with him. You made him suffer and then you left him. You could not love him, because you are too proud… no, not proud, my mistake, but because you are vain… perhaps not even that. You are selfish to the point of… insanity, and your letters addressed to me are proof enough of that. You could never have fallen in love with him, simple as he is, and perhaps deep down you even hated and mocked him. The only thing you could love was your own infamy and the ever-present realization that you’d been disgraced and insulted. Had you less infamy to contend with, or none at all, you’d have been more unhappy…” (Aglaya delighted in rolling off her tongue all these carefully considered and rehearsed charges, considered and rehearsed way back, at a time when in her wildest dreams she could not have foreseen the present encounter. With eyes brimming with venom, she observed the effect her words had on Nastasya Filippovna’s pain-wracked features.) “You will recall,” she continued, “he wrote me a letter then. He tells me you knew about the letter and had even read it. This letter made everything clear to me, and I was right. He recently confirmed it to me himself, that is, what I told you just now, word for word. After I received the letter, I began to wait. I was right in thinking you’d come here, because you’d miss St Petersburg too much. You are still too young and too beautiful for life in the provinces… Incidentally, these are not my words either,” she added, blushing to the roots of her hair, and from this moment on her face remained flushed till the very end of her speech. “After I saw the Prince again, I felt a fresh wave of sorrow and pity for him. Do not laugh. If you laugh, it will make you unworthy of appreciating what I have—”

Here, then, is my reply to all your letters: I began to feel sorry for Prince Lev Nikolayevich on the very day that I made his acquaintance, and when I later learned of all that happened at your soiree. I felt sorry for him, as he is such a simple-hearted man who, because of his simplicity, believed that he could be happy ... with a woman ... of that character. What I feared would happen to him did indeed happen: you were unable to love him, you tormented and abandoned him. You couldn’t love him because you’re too proud ... no, not proud, I was wrong, but because you’re vain ... not even that: you are self-loving to the point of ... insanity, of which your letters to me may serve as proof. You couldn’t love him, such a simple man, and you even, perhaps, privately despised and ridiculed him, could love only your own disgrace and the constant thought that you were disgraced and that you’d been humiliated. source_text: — Вы не так поняли, — сказала она, — я с вами не пришла... ссориться, хотя я вас не люблю. Я... я пришла к вам... с человеческою речью. Призывая вас, я уже решила, о чем буду вам говорить, и от решения не отступлюсь, хотя бы вы и совсем меня не поняли. Тем для вас будет хуже, а не для меня. Я хотела вам ответить на то, что вы мне писали, и ответить лично, потому что мне это казалось удобнее. Выслушайте же мой ответ на все ваши письма: мне стало жаль князя Льва Николаевича в первый раз в тот самый день, когда я с ним познакомилась и когда потом узнала обо всем, что произошло на вашем вечере. Мне потому его стало жаль, что он такой простодушный человек и по простоте своей поверил, что может быть счастлив... с женщиной... такого характера. Чего я боялась за него, то и случилось: вы не могли его полюбить, измучили его и кинули. Вы потому его не могли любить, что слишком горды... нет, не горды, я ошиблась, а потому, что вы тщеславны... даже и не это: вы себялюбивы до... сумасшествия, чему доказательством служат и ваши письма ко мне. Вы его, такого простого, не могли полюбить, и даже, может быть, про себя презирали и смеялись над ним, могли полюбить только один свой позор и беспрерывную мысль о том, что вы опозорены и что вас оскорбили. Будь у вас меньше позору или не будь его вовсе, вы были бы несчастнее... (Аглая с наслаждением выговаривала эти слишком уж поспешно выскакивавшие, но давно уже приготовленные и обдуманные слова, тогда еще обдуманные, когда и во сне не представлялось теперешнего свидания; она ядовитым взглядом следила за эффектом их на искаженном от волнения лице Настасьи Филипповны). Вы помните, — продолжала она, — тогда он написал мне письмо; он говорит, что вы про это письмо знаете и даже читали его? По этому письму я всё поняла, и верно поняла; он недавно мне подтвердил это сам, то есть всё, что я теперь вам говорю, слово в слово даже. После письма я стала ждать. Я угадала, что вы должны приехать сюда, потому что вам нельзя же быть без Петербурга: вы еще слишком молоды и хороши собой для провинции... Впрочем, это тоже не мои слова, — прибавила она, ужасно покраснев, и с этой минуты краска уже не сходила с ее лица, вплоть до самого окончания речи. — Когда я увидала опять князя, мне стало ужасно за него больно и обидно. Не смейтесь; если вы будете смеяться, то вы недостойны это понять...

source_text: — Вы не так поняли, — сказала она, — я с вами не пришла... ссориться, хотя я вас не люблю. Я... я пришла к вам... с человеческою речью. Призывая вас, я уже решила, о чем буду вам говорить, и от решения не отступлюсь, хотя бы вы и совсем меня не поняли. Тем для вас будет хуже, а не для меня. Я хотела вам ответить на то, что вы мне писали, и ответить лично, потому что мне это казалось удобнее. Выслушайте же мой ответ на все ваши письма: мне стало жаль князя Льва Николаевича в первый раз в тот самый день, когда я с ним познакомилась и когда потом узнала обо всем, что произошло на вашем вечере. Мне потому его стало жаль, что он такой простодушный человек и по простоте своей поверил, что может быть счастлив... с женщиной... такого характера. Чего я боялась за него, то и случилось: вы не могли его полюбить, измучили его и кинули. Вы потому его не могли любить, что слишком горды... нет, не горды, я ошиблась, а потому, что вы тщеславны... даже и не это: вы себялюбивы до... сумасшествия, чему доказательством служат и ваши письма ко мне. Вы его, такого простого, не могли полюбить, и даже, может быть, про себя презирали и смеялись над ним, могли полюбить только один свой позор и беспрерывную мысль о том, что вы опозорены и что вас оскорбили. Будь у вас меньше позору или не будь его вовсе, вы были бы несчастнее... (Аглая с наслаждением выговаривала эти слишком уж поспешно выскакивавшие, но давно уже приготовленные и обдуманные слова, тогда еще обдуманные, когда и во сне не представлялось теперешнего свидания; она ядовитым взглядом следила за эффектом их на искаженном от волнения лице Настасьи Филипповны). Вы помните, — продолжала она, — тогда он написал мне письмо; он говорит, что вы про это письмо знаете и даже читали его? По этому письму я всё поняла, и верно поняла; он недавно мне подтвердил это сам, то есть всё, что я теперь вам говорю, слово в слово даже. После письма я стала ждать. Я угадала, что вы должны приехать сюда, потому что вам нельзя же быть без Петербурга: вы еще слишком молоды и хороши собой для провинции... Впрочем, это тоже не мои слова, — прибавила она, ужасно покраснев, и с этой минуты краска уже не сходила с ее лица, вплоть до самого окончания речи. — Когда я увидала опять князя, мне стало ужасно за него больно и обидно. Не смейтесь; если вы будете смеяться, то вы недостойны это понять...

In calling upon you, I had already decided what I was going to say to you, and shall not deviate from my resolution even if you failed to understand me totally. I felt sorry for him because he is such a simple-hearted man, and in his simplicity had supposed he could be happy… with a woman… with such a character. What I feared would happen to him has happened. You could not fall in love with him. You made him suffer and then you left him. You could not love him, because you are too proud… no, not proud, my mistake, but because you are vain… perhaps not even that. translation: You see the Monkey King splitting the waterway, straight back to the Iron Board Bridge, leaping up. Only to see four old monkeys, leading the other monkeys: all waiting by the bridge. Suddenly, they saw Sun Wukong jump out of the waves, not a speck of water on him, golden and radiant, walking onto the bridge. The monkeys were all frightened and knelt down, saying, "King, what splendid colors! What splendid colors!" Sun Wukong, with a pleasant smile, climbed onto the throne, holding the iron rod in the middle. The other monkeys, unaware of their manners, all came to grab that treasure, but it was like a dragonfly trying to shake an iron tree; they couldn't budge it at all. They all bit their fingers and stuck out their tongues, saying, "Grandfather! So heavy, how did you manage to bring it?" Sun Wukong approached, stretched out his hand, and grabbed it, laughing and saying, "Every object has its owner. This treasure was sealed in the ocean for thousands of years, and just so happened to shine brightly this year. The Dragon King thought it was just a piece of black iron and called it the divine treasure at the bottom of the天河. None of those fellows could lift it, so they asked me to go and take it. At that time, the treasure was over two丈long and as thick as a bushel; I grabbed it, thought it was too big, and it became much smaller; when I asked for it to be smaller, it became even smaller; when I asked for it to be smaller again, it became even smaller. Hurrying to look at the light, it had a line of characters on top: '如意金箍棒, 一万三千五百斤.' All of you step back, and let me show you how it can change again." He tossed the treasure in his hand, saying, "Smaller! Smaller! Smaller!" Instantly, it became as small as a needle for embroidery, which could be stuffed inside the ear. The monkeys were startled, calling out, "King, give it back for us to play with!" Sun Wukong really went into his ear and took it out, holding it in his palm, calling, "Bigger! Bigger! Bigger!" Immediately, it grew to the size of a bushel and two丈long. In the joy of his demonstration, he leaped onto the bridge, walked out of the cave, held the treasure in his hand, used his celestial mimicry divine power, and bent his waist, calling, "Long!" And he grew to ten thousand feet, his head like a mountain, waist like a steep mountain, eyes like lightning, mouth like a blood basin, and teeth like swords and spears. In his hand, that rod touched the thirty-three heavens above and reached the eighteen layers of hell below, frightening all the tigers, leopards, wolves, and foxes, all the creatures of the mountain, the seventy-two cave kings, to prostrate and greet. In an instant, he gathered his power, changed the treasure back to a needle for embroidery, and hid it in his ear, returning to his cave. All the cave kings were terrified and came to congratulate him.
source_text: 你看这猴王，分开水道，径回铁板桥头，撺将上去，只见四个老猴，领着众猴：都在桥边等待。忽然见悟空跳出波外，身上更无一点水湿，金灿灿的，走上桥来。唬得众猴一齐跪下道：“大王，好华彩耶！好华彩耶！”悟空满面春风，高登宝座，将铁棒竖在当中。那些猴不知好歹，都来拿那宝贝，却便似蜻蜓撼铁树，分毫也不能禁动。一个个咬指伸舌道：“爷爷呀！这般重，亏你怎的拿来也！”悟空近前，舒开手，一把挝起，对众笑道：“物各有主。这宝贝镇于海藏中，也不知几千百年，可可的今岁放光。龙王只认做是块黑铁，又唤做天河镇底神珍。那厮每都扛不动，请我亲去拿之。那时此宝有二丈多长，斗来粗细；被我挝他一把，意思嫌大，他就少了许多；再教小些，他又小了许多；再教小些，他又小了许多；急对天光看处，上有一行字，乃‘如意金箍棒，一万三千五百斤。’你都站开，等我再叫他变一变看。”他将那宝贝颠在手中，叫：“小！小！小！”即时就小做一个绣花针儿相似，可以塞在耳朵里面藏下。众猴骇然，叫道：“大王！还拿出来耍耍！”猴王真个去耳朵里拿出，托放掌上叫：“大！大！大！”即又大做斗来粗细，二丈长短。他弄到欢喜处，跳上桥，走出洞外，将宝贝攥在手中，使一个法天像地的神通，把腰一躬，叫声“长！”他就长的高万丈，头如泰山，腰如峻岭，眼如闪电，口似血盆，牙如剑戟；手中那棒，上抵三十三天，下至十八层地狱，把些虎豹狼虫，满山群怪，七十二洞妖王，都唬得磕头拜礼，战兢兢魄散魂飞。霎时收了法像，将宝贝还变做个绣花针儿，藏在耳内，复归洞府。慌得那各洞妖王，都来参贺。

human_translations.translator_1: Look at that Monkey King! He opened up the waterway and went straight back to the head of the sheet iron bridge. The four old monkeys were leading the other monkeys and waiting beside the bridge. They suddenly beheld Wukong leaping out of the waves: there was not a drop of water on his body as he walked onto the bridge, all radiant and golden. The various monkeys were so astonished that they all knelt down, crying, “ Great King, what marvels! What marvels!” Beaming broadly, Wukong ascended his high throne and set up the iron rod right in the center. Not knowing any better, the monkeys all came and tried to pick the treasure up. It was rather like a dragonfly attempting to shake an ironwood tree: they could not budge it an inch! Biting their fingers and sticking out their tongues, every one of them said, “O Father, it’s so heavy! How did you ever manage to bring it here?” Wukong walked up to the rod, stretched forth his hands, and picked it up. Laughing, he said to them, “Everything has its owner. This treasure has presided in the ocean treasury for who knows how many thousands of years, and it just happened to glow recently. The Dragon King only recognized it as a piece of black iron, though it is also said to be the divine rarity which fixed the bottom of the Heavenly River. All those fellows together could not lift or move it, and they asked me to take it myself. At first, this treasure was more than twenty feet long and as thick as a barrel. After I struck it once and expressed my feeling that it was too large, it grew smaller. I wanted it smaller still, and again it grew smaller. For a third time I commanded it, and it grew smaller still! When I looked at it in the light, it had on it the inscription, ‘The Compliant Golden-Hooped Rod. Weight: thirteen thousand five hundred pounds.’ Stand aside, all of you. Let me ask it to go through some more transformations.” He held the treasure in his hands and called out, “Smaller, smaller, smaller!” and at once it shrank to the size of a tiny embroidery needle, small enough to be hidden inside the ear. Awestruck, the monkeys cried, “Great King! Take it out and play with it some more.” The Monkey King took it out from his ear and placed it on his palm. “Bigger, bigger, bigger!” he shouted, and again it grew to the thickness of a barrel and more than twenty feet long. He became so delighted playing with it that he jumped onto the bridge and walked out of the cave. Grasping the treasure in his hands, he began to perform the magic of cosmic imitation. Bending over, he cried, “Grow!” and at once grew to be ten thousand feet tall, with a head like the Tai Mountain and a chest like a rugged peak, eyes like lightning and a mouth like a blood bowl, and teeth like swords and halberds. The rod in his hands was of such a size that its top reached the thirty-third Heaven and its bottom the eighteenth layer of Hell. Tigers, leopards, wolves, and crawling creatures, all the monsters of the mountain and the demon kings of the seventy-two caves, were so terrified that they kowtowed and paid homage to the Monkey King in fear and trembling. Presently he revoked his magical appearance and changed the treasure back into a tiny embroidery needle stored in his ear. He returned to the cave dwelling, but the demon kings of the various caves were still frightened, and they continued to come to pay their respects.
human_translations.translator_2: The four Sea Kings were greatly displeased at this and discussed how they might memorialize about the matter. But the Monkey King looked for his waterway in order to get back to the top of the iron bridge in his cave. All the monkeys were there gathered, waiting for him. Suddenly their king jumped out of the water, with not a drop of water left on him, and landed on the iron bridge. At the sight all the monkeys were greatly frightened, and fell on their knees saying, “Great King, how beautifully dressed you are.” The Monkey King was mightily pleased and ascended a high throne. He took the iron beam and made it stand on end in their midst. The monkeys were all full of wonder and came round to feel that precious beam, but their strength was like that of flies, and they could not move it the least bit. They all put out their tongues and cried, “Aiyah! Aiyah! It is terribly heavy. How did you manage to bring it? Such a tremendous weight!” The Seeker of Secrets came up, took it in his hand, and smiled at them. “Everything has a master, so has this precious beam. It has been lying in the storehouse of the sea, who knows for how many thousands of years. His loins were as great as mountain ridges, his eyes like lightning, his mouth like a bucket of blood, his teeth like sharp spears. He then took the magic lance in his hand, which reached up to the 33rd heaven and down to the 18 hells, frightening the 72 demon kings in hell, so that they all kowtowed to him in fear and trembling. human_translations.translator_3: Parting the waters again, Monkey swept back onto the iron bridge, where his subjects were eagerly awaiting his return. When they saw their king suddenly leap out of the waves, perfectly dry and in his glittering new costume, they kneeled in awe. Monkey sat triumphantly on his throne with the iron staff propped up before him. Not knowing any better, his monkeys crowded around, anxious to try it themselves. Like dragonflies trying to shake a tree, they couldn’t move it even a fraction of an inch. “How did Your Majesty carry it all the way here?” they chattered in wonder. “Every object has its master,” said Monkey, smiling and picking it up. “For thousands of years, this piece of iron lay in the ocean treasury fixing the depth of the Heavenly River until, a few days ago, it began giving off light. It has a name—the Obedient Golden-Hooped Staff—and it does whatever I say. When I first laid eyes on it, it was fifty feet long and as thick as a barrel, but it shrank as soon as I told it to. Stand to one side, while I tell it to transform. Smaller!” In an instant, the staff had shrunk to the size of an embroidery needle, which Monkey tucked inside his ear. “More magic!” bayed the amazed monkeys. Their king placed the staff on the palm of his hand: “Bigger!” he shouted. It immediately became a twenty-foot pillar that was a couple of feet in diameter. Monkey now tried a touch of cosmic imitation. Bounding out of the cave, he cried “Grow!” and promptly shot up to one hundred thousand feet tall. His head resembled the craggy summit of Mount Tai, with flashing eyes and a butcher’s-bowl mouth full of razor teeth. His staff reached up to the thirty-third story of Heaven, and down to the eighteenth level of Hell. Tigers, leopards, wolves, snakes, and the demon kings of the seventy-two caves all emerged to kowtow in terror. A moment later, Monkey undid the magic, shrank the staff down to the size of a needle, tucked it inside his ear again, and sashayed back inside the cave.
human_translations.translator_4: Watch the Monkey King as he parts the waters and goes straight back to the iron bridge, where the four senior apes can be seen waiting for him at the head of the monkey host. Sun Wukong suddenly leapt out of the waves without a drop of water on him and gleaming with gold. As he came across the bridge the monkeys were so astonished that they fell to their knees and said, “How splendid you look, Your Majesty, how splendid.” Sun Wukong, his face lit up with youthful vigor, climbed up to his throne, thrust his cudgel into the ground in their midst. The foolish monkeys all tried to grab this treasure, but it was as futile as a dragonfly trying to shake an iron tree : they were unable to move it in the slightest. Biting their fingers and sticking out their tongues they said, “Grandpa, it's so heavy, how can you possibly lift it?” Sun Wukong went over, lifted it with one hand, and laughed as he said to them, “Everything has its rightful owner. This little treasure has been lying in the sea treasury for goodness knows how many thousands of years, but it just happened to start shining this year. The Dragon King thought it was just a piece of ordinary iron, and said it was the miraculous treasure that holds the bed of the Milky Way in place. None of his men could move it, so he had to ask me to go and fetch it myself. It was more than twenty feet long then, and as thick as a peck-measure. When I picked it up I felt that it was too big, and it shrank till it was several times as small. I told it to get even smaller, and it did that too; then I told it to get smaller still, and it got many times smaller again. I hurried out into the light of day to look at it, and I saw that there was an inscription on it that read 'AS-YOU-WILL GOLD-BANDED CUDGEL: WEIGHT 13,500 POUNDS'. Stand aside, and I'll make it change again.” Holding his treasure in his hand he said, “Shrink, shrink, shrink,” and it became as small as an embroidery needle, tiny enough to be hidden in his ear. “Your Majesty,” the monkeys cried out in astonishment, “bring it out and play with it again.” So the Monkey King brought it out of his ear again, laid it on the palm of his hand, and said, “Grow, grow, grow.” It became as thick as a peck again and twenty feet long. Now that he was really enjoying himself he bounded over the bridge and went out of the cave. Clasping his treasure he used some of his heaven and earth magic, bowed, and shouted, “Grow.” He became a hundred thousand feet tall; his head was as big as a mountain, his waist like a range of hills, his eyes flashed like lightning, his mouth seemed to be a bowl of blood, and his teeth were as swords and halberds; the cudgel in his hands reached up to the Thirty-third Heaven and down to the Eighteenth Hell. The tigers, leopards and wolves, the beasts of the mountain, and the seventy-two monster kings all kowtowed and bowed in terror, trembling so much that they went out of their minds. A moment later he reverted to his proper size, turned his treasure into an embroidery needle, hid it in his ear, and went back to the cave. The panic-stricken kings of the monsters all came to offer their congratulations.

translation:
You see, the King of Monkeys split the waterway and returned to the iron plate bridgehead, darting up onto it. There, the four older monkeys led by the others stood at the bridge, waiting. Suddenly, they saw Monkey King jump out of the waves, his body completely dry, golden and radiant, walking onto the bridge. This frightened the other monkeys, who all knelt down in unison and cried, "Great King! What splendid luster! What splendid luster!" Monkey King, beaming, ascended the throne, erecting his magic rod in the center. The monkeys, not knowing how to behave, all tried to grab the treasure, but it was as if a dragonfly were trying to shake a cypress tree—impossible to move it. They all bit their fingers and stuck out their tongues, exclaiming, "Grandfather! So heavy! How did you manage to bring it?"

Monkey King advanced, stretched out his hands, and picked up the rod, smiling as he said, "Every object has its owner. This treasure has lain hidden at the bottom of the sea for thousands of years. Only this year did it emit light. The dragon kings thought it was just a lump of black iron, calling it the divine treasure at the bottom of the天河. None of them could lift it, so they asked me to go get it. At the time, the rod was over two zhang long, as thick as a choushi (a measurement), and quite heavy. When I grabbed it, I felt it was too big and made it smaller. When I asked for it to be even smaller, it became smaller. When I asked for it to be even smaller, it became even smaller. When I looked at it under the light, I saw a line of characters that read, '如意金箍棒, 一万三千五百斤.' Step back, and let me show you how it can change again." He shook the rod in his hands and shouted, "Smaller! Smaller! Smaller!" Instantly, it shrank to the size of a sewing needle, able to be hidden inside an ear. The monkeys were startled and cried, "Great King! Please show it to us again!" Monkey King really took the rod out of his ear, held it in his palm, and shouted, "Larger! Larger! Larger!" It grew to the size of a dou (measurement), and two zhang long. When he was in a jovial mood, he jumped onto the bridge, walked out to the cave entrance, and held the rod in his hand. Using his divine power to transform, he bent his waist and said, "Grow!" He grew to a height of ten thousand feet, his head like Mount Tai, his waist like a steep ridge, his eyes like lightning, his mouth like a blood bowl, his teeth like swords. The rod in his hand reached the thirty-third heaven at the top and the eighteen levels of hell at the bottom. It frightened tigers, leopards, wolves, foxes, and other beasts, as well as all the monkeys in the mountain, the seventy-two cave kings, who all knelt and bowed, trembling in fear. In an instant, he retracted his divine form and restored the rod to the size of a sewing needle, which he hid in his ear, returning to the cave. The various cave kings were alarmed and hurried to congratulate him.

human_translations.translator_1: Look at that Monkey King! He opened up the waterway and went straight back to the head of the sheet iron bridge. The four old monkeys were leading the other monkeys and waiting beside the bridge. They suddenly beheld Wukong leaping out of the waves: there was not a drop of water on his body as he walked onto the bridge, all radiant and golden. The various monkeys were so astonished that they all knelt down, crying, “ Great King, what marvels! What marvels!” Beaming broadly, Wukong ascended his high throne and set up the iron rod right in the center. Not knowing any better, the monkeys all came and tried to pick the treasure up. It was rather like a dragonfly attempting to shake an ironwood tree: they could not budge it an inch! Biting their fingers and sticking out their tongues, every one of them said, “O Father, it’s so heavy! How did you ever manage to bring it here?” Wukong walked up to the rod, stretched forth his hands, and picked it up. Laughing, he said to them, “Everything has its owner. This treasure has presided in the ocean treasury for who knows how many thousands of years, and it just happened to glow recently. The Dragon King only recognized it as a piece of black iron, though it is also said to be the divine rarity which fixed the bottom of the Heavenly River. All those fellows together could not lift or move it, and they asked me to take it myself. At first, this treasure was more than twenty feet long and as thick as a barrel. After I struck it once and expressed my feeling that it was too large, it grew smaller. I wanted it smaller still, and again it grew smaller. For a third time I commanded it, and it grew smaller still! When I looked at it in the light, it had on it the inscription, ‘The Compliant Golden-Hooped Rod. Weight: thirteen thousand five hundred pounds.’ Stand aside, all of you. Let me ask it to go through some more transformations.” He held the treasure in his hands and called out, “Smaller, smaller, smaller!” and at once it shrank to the size of a tiny embroidery needle, small enough to be hidden inside the ear. Awestruck, the monkeys cried, “Great King! Take it out and play with it some more.” The Monkey King took it out from his ear and placed it on his palm. “Bigger, bigger, bigger!” he shouted, and again it grew to the thickness of a barrel and more than twenty feet long. He became so delighted playing with it that he jumped onto the bridge and walked out of the cave. Grasping the treasure in his hands, he began to perform the magic of cosmic imitation. Bending over, he cried, “Grow!” and at once grew to be ten thousand feet tall, with a head like the Tai Mountain and a chest like a rugged peak, eyes like lightning and a mouth like a blood bowl, and teeth like swords and halberds. The rod in his hands was of such a size that its top reached the thirty-third Heaven and its bottom the eighteenth layer of Hell. Tigers, leopards, wolves, and crawling creatures, all the monsters of the mountain and the demon kings of the seventy-two caves, were so terrified that they kowtowed and paid homage to the Monkey King in fear and trembling. Presently he revoked his magical appearance and changed the treasure back into a tiny embroidery needle stored in his ear. He returned to the cave dwelling, but the demon kings of the various caves were still frightened, and they continued to come to pay their respects.
human_translations.translator_2: The four Sea Kings were greatly displeased at this and discussed how they might memorialize about the matter. But the Monkey King looked for his waterway in order to get back to the top of the iron bridge in his cave. All the monkeys were there gathered, waiting for him. Suddenly their king jumped out of the water, with not a drop of water left on him, and landed on the iron bridge. At the sight all the monkeys were greatly frightened, and fell on their knees saying, “Great King, how beautifully dressed you are.” The Monkey King was mightily pleased and ascended a high throne. He took the iron beam and made it stand on end in their midst. The monkeys were all full of wonder and came round to feel that precious beam, but their strength was like that of flies, and they could not move it the least bit. They all put out their tongues and cried, “Aiyah! Aiyah! It is terribly heavy. How did you manage to bring it? Such a tremendous weight!” The Seeker of Secrets came up, took it in his hand, and smiled at them. “Everything has a master, so has this precious beam. It has been lying in the storehouse of the sea, who knows for how many thousands of years. But just when I was there, it emitted light in all directions, and the Dragon King thought it only a bit of black iron. But it was called the Pearl of the River of Heaven. None of the people there could move it, so they asked me to go and take it. At that time this precious beam was more than twenty feet long, and stouter than a bushel measure. When I looked at it, I thought it was too big, then suddenly it became less. I thought it still too big, and again it became much less. On it are engraved a few words, “As You Like It.” All of you stand back and I will command it to change, so that you can see what it will do in my hand. When I say ‘Small, Small, Small,’ instantly it becomes the size of an embroidery needle, so that I can hide it in my ear.” And so it was. All the monkeys were greatly astonished and said, “Oh Great King, show us how you handle it.” The Monkey King took it from his ear, put it on the palm of his hand and cried, “Big, Big, Big.” Instantly it became as a bushel measure in thickness and twenty feet long. He took it in his hand with great joy, jumped outside the cave with it, and then exercised his own magic on it. He doubled up his back and cried out, “High, High, High.” In an instant he was 100,000 feet tall, and his head was as high as the peak of Mount Tai. His loins were as great as mountain ridges, his eyes like lightning, his mouth like a bucket of blood, his teeth like sharp spears. He then took the magic lance in his hand, which reached up to the 33rd heaven and down to the 18 hells, frightening the 72 demon kings in hell, so that they all kowtowed to him in fear and trembling. In the twinkling of an eye, he took the precious lance, changed it by magic to the size of an embroidery needle, and hid it in his ear, and then returned to his cave. After this, all the demon kings came to pay homage to him.
human_translations.translator_3: Parting the waters again, Monkey swept back onto the iron bridge, where his subjects were eagerly awaiting his return. When they saw their king suddenly leap out of the waves, perfectly dry and in his glittering new costume, they kneeled in awe. Monkey sat triumphantly on his throne with the iron staff propped up before him. Not knowing any better, his monkeys crowded around, anxious to try it themselves. Like dragonflies trying to shake a tree, they couldn’t move it even a fraction of an inch. “How did Your Majesty carry it all the way here?” they chattered in wonder. “Every object has its master,” said Monkey, smiling and picking it up. “For thousands of years, this piece of iron lay in the ocean treasury fixing the depth of the Heavenly River until, a few days ago, it began giving off light. It has a name—the Obedient Golden-Hooped Staff—and it does whatever I say. When I first laid eyes on it, it was fifty feet long and as thick as a barrel, but it shrank as soon as I told it to. Stand to one side, while I tell it to transform. Smaller!” In an instant, the staff had shrunk to the size of an embroidery needle, which Monkey tucked inside his ear. “More magic!” bayed the amazed monkeys. Their king placed the staff on the palm of his hand: “Bigger!” he shouted. It immediately became a twenty-foot pillar that was a couple of feet in diameter. Monkey now tried a touch of cosmic imitation. Bounding out of the cave, he cried “Grow!” and promptly shot up to one hundred thousand feet tall. His head resembled the craggy summit of Mount Tai, with flashing eyes and a butcher’s-bowl mouth full of razor teeth. His staff reached up to the thirty-third story of Heaven, and down to the eighteenth level of Hell. Tigers, leopards, wolves, snakes, and the demon kings of the seventy-two caves all emerged to kowtow in terror. A moment later, Monkey undid the magic, shrank the staff down to the size of a needle, tucked it inside his ear again, and sashayed back inside the cave.
human_translations.translator_4: Watch the Monkey King as he parts the waters and goes straight back to the iron bridge, where the four senior apes can be seen waiting for him at the head of the monkey host. Sun Wukong suddenly leapt out of the waves without a drop of water on him and gleaming with gold. As he came across the bridge the monkeys were so astonished that they fell to their knees and said, “How splendid you look, Your Majesty, how splendid.” Sun Wukong, his face lit up with youthful vigor, climbed up to his throne, thrust his cudgel into the ground in their midst. The foolish monkeys all tried to grab this treasure, but it was as futile as a dragonfly trying to shake an iron tree : they were unable to move it in the slightest. Biting their fingers and sticking out their tongues they said, “Grandpa, it's so heavy, how can you possibly lift it?” Sun Wukong went over, lifted it with one hand, and laughed as he said to them, “Everything has its rightful owner. This little treasure has been lying in the sea treasury for goodness knows how many thousands of years, but it just happened to start shining this year. The Dragon King thought it was just a piece of ordinary iron, and said it was the miraculous treasure that holds the bed of the Milky Way in place. None of his men could move it, so he had to ask me to go and fetch it myself. It was more than twenty feet long then, and as thick as a peck-measure. When I picked it up I felt that it was too big, and it shrank till it was several times as small. I told it to get even smaller, and it did that too; then I told it to get smaller still, and it got many times smaller again. I hurried out into the light of day to look at it, and I saw that there was an inscription on it that read 'AS-YOU-WILL GOLD-BANDED CUDGEL: WEIGHT 13,500 POUNDS'. Stand aside, and I'll make it change again.” Holding his treasure in his hand he said, “Shrink, shrink, shrink,” and it became as small as an embroidery needle, tiny enough to be hidden in his ear. “Your Majesty,” the monkeys cried out in astonishment, “bring it out and play with it again.” So the Monkey King brought it out of his ear again, laid it on the palm of his hand, and said, “Grow, grow, grow.” It became as thick as a peck again and twenty feet long. Now that he was really enjoying himself he bounded over the bridge and went out of the cave. Clasping his treasure he used some of his heaven and earth magic, bowed, and shouted, “Grow.” He became a hundred thousand feet tall; his head was as big as a mountain, his waist like a range of hills, his eyes flashed like lightning, his mouth seemed to be a bowl of blood, and his teeth were as swords and halberds; the cudgel in his hands reached up to the Thirty-third Heaven and down to the Eighteenth Hell. The tigers, leopards and wolves, the beasts of the mountain, and the seventy-two monster kings all kowtowed and bowed in terror, trembling so much that they went out of their minds. A moment later he reverted to his proper size, turned his treasure into an embroidery needle, hid it in his ear, and went back to the cave. The panic-stricken kings of the monsters all came to offer their congratulations.

translation: You see this monkey king split the waterway and proceed directly back to the Iron Plate Bridge, leaping up onto it. He sees four old monkeys leading the other monkeys, all waiting at the edge of the bridge. Suddenly, they see Wukong jump out of the waves, his body dry as if he had never been wet, glistening golden. He walks onto the bridge, terrifying the other monkeys who all kneel down. They cry out, "King, how splendid! How splendid!" Wukong, his face smiling, ascends the throne, holding his iron rod in the center. The monkeys, unaware of his true strength, all attempt to seize the treasure, only to find it as inedible as a dragonfly trying to shake a tree; it cannot be moved. They bite their fingers and stick out their tongues, saying, "Grandfather! It's so heavy, how did you bring it?" Wukong steps forward, stretches out his hand, and picks up the treasure, smiling at the gathered monkeys. "Every object has its owner. This treasure was sealed in the ocean for thousands of years, and only now is it shining. The Dragon King thought it was just a block of black iron and called it the Divine Treasure at the Bottom of the Heavenly River. None of them could move it, so they asked me to fetch it myself. Then, this treasure was over two dozen feet long and as thick as a ladle. I took it with one hand, found it too big, so I made it smaller; I made it smaller, and it became even smaller; I made it smaller, and it became even smaller. Just when I glanced at it in the sunlight, it bore the inscription: '如意金箍棒，一万三千五百斤.' You all step back, and let me show you how it can change." He tosses the treasure in his hand and calls, "Smaller! Smaller! Smaller!" Instantly, it becomes as small as a needle for embroidery, fitting inside an ear. The monkeys are startled, calling out, "King, bring it out and play with it!" The monkey king indeed pulls it out of his ear, placing it in his palm. He calls, "Bigger! Bigger! Bigger!" And it becomes as thick as a ladle, measuring over two dozen feet. Enraptured by the spectacle, he leaps onto the bridge, walks out of the cave, and holds the treasure in his hand, employing his divine power to transform his body. He bends his waist and calls, "Grow!" and he grows to a height of ten thousand feet, his head like a mountain, his waist like a mountain ridge, his eyes like lightning, his mouth like a blood basin, and his teeth like swords. His hand holds the rod, reaching to the thirty-third heaven and descending to the eighteenth level of hell, terrifying the tigers, leopards, wolves, and foxes, all the beasts of the mountain, and the seventy-two cave demon kings, who all fall to their knees in reverence and flee in terror. Instantly, he retracts his divine form, and the treasure returns to its original size, fitting inside his ear. All the cave demon kings rush to congratulate him in panic.

But just when I was there, it emitted light in all directions, and the Dragon King thought it only a bit of black iron. But it was called the Pearl of the River of Heaven. None of the people there could move it, so they asked me to go and take it. At that time this precious beam was more than twenty feet long, and stouter than a bushel measure. When I looked at it, I thought it was too big, then suddenly it became less. I thought it still too big, and again it became much less. On it are engraved a few words, “As You Like It.” All of you stand back and I will command it to change, so that you can see what it will do in my hand. When I say ‘Small, Small, Small,’ instantly it becomes the size of an embroidery needle, so that I can hide it in my ear.” And so it was. All the monkeys were greatly astonished and said, “Oh Great King, show us how you handle it.” The Monkey King took it from his ear, put it on the palm of his hand and cried, “Big, Big, Big.” Instantly it became as a bushel measure in thickness and twenty feet long. He took it in his hand with great joy, jumped outside the cave with it, and then exercised his own magic on it. He doubled up his back and cried out, “High, High, High.” In an instant he was 100,000 feet tall, and his head was as high as the peak of Mount Tai. His loins were as great as mountain ridges, his eyes like lightning, his mouth like a bucket of blood, his teeth like sharp spears. He then took the magic lance in his hand, which reached up to the 33rd heaven and down to the 18 hells, frightening the 72 demon kings in hell, so that they all kowtowed to him in fear and trembling. In the twinkling of an eye, he took the precious lance, changed it by magic to the size of an embroidery needle, and hid it in his ear, and then returned to his cave. After this, all the demon kings came to pay homage to him.
human_translations.translator_3: Parting the waters again, Monkey swept back onto the iron bridge, where his subjects were eagerly awaiting his return. When they saw their king suddenly leap out of the waves, perfectly dry and in his glittering new costume, they kneeled in awe. Monkey sat triumphantly on his throne with the iron staff propped up before him. Not knowing any better, his monkeys crowded around, anxious to try it themselves. Like dragonflies trying to shake a tree, they couldn’t move it even a fraction of an inch. “How did Your Majesty carry it all the way here?” they chattered in wonder. “Every object has its master,” said Monkey, smiling and picking it up. “For thousands of years, this piece of iron lay in the ocean treasury fixing the depth of the Heavenly River until, a few days ago, it began giving off light. It has a name—the Obedient Golden-Hooped Staff—and it does whatever I say. When I first laid eyes on it, it was fifty feet long and as thick as a barrel, but it shrank as soon as I told it to. Stand to one side, while I tell it to transform. Smaller!” In an instant, the staff had shrunk to the size of an embroidery needle, which Monkey tucked inside his ear. “More magic!” bayed the amazed monkeys. Their king placed the staff on the palm of his hand: “Bigger!” he shouted. It immediately became a twenty-foot pillar that was a couple of feet in diameter. Monkey now tried a touch of cosmic imitation. Bounding out of the cave, he cried “Grow!” and promptly shot up to one hundred thousand feet tall. His head resembled the craggy summit of Mount Tai, with flashing eyes and a butcher’s-bowl mouth full of razor teeth. His staff reached up to the thirty-third story of Heaven, and down to the eighteenth level of Hell. Tigers, leopards, wolves, snakes, and the demon kings of the seventy-two caves all emerged to kowtow in terror. A moment later, Monkey undid the magic, shrank the staff down to the size of a needle, tucked it inside his ear again, and sashayed back inside the cave.
human_translations.translator_4: Watch the Monkey King as he parts the waters and goes straight back to the iron bridge, where the four senior apes can be seen waiting for him at the head of the monkey host. Sun Wukong suddenly leapt out of the waves without a drop of water on him and gleaming with gold. As he came across the bridge the monkeys were so astonished that they fell to their knees and said, “How splendid you look, Your Majesty, how splendid.” Sun Wukong, his face lit up with youthful vigor, climbed up to his throne, thrust his cudgel into the ground in their midst. The foolish monkeys all tried to grab this treasure, but it was as futile as a dragonfly trying to shake an iron tree : they were unable to move it in the slightest. Biting their fingers and sticking out their tongues they said, “Grandpa, it's so heavy, how can you possibly lift it?” Sun Wukong went over, lifted it with one hand, and laughed as he said to them, “Everything has its rightful owner. This little treasure has been lying in the sea treasury for goodness knows how many thousands of years, but it just happened to start shining this year. The Dragon King thought it was just a piece of ordinary iron, and said it was the miraculous treasure that holds the bed of the Milky Way in place. None of his men could move it, so he had to ask me to go and fetch it myself. It was more than twenty feet long then, and as thick as a peck-measure. When I picked it up I felt that it was too big, and it shrank till it was several times as small. I told it to get even smaller, and it did that too; then I told it to get smaller still, and it got many times smaller again. I hurried out into the light of day to look at it, and I saw that there was an inscription on it that read 'AS-YOU-WILL GOLD-BANDED CUDGEL: WEIGHT 13,500 POUNDS'. Stand aside, and I'll make it change again.” Holding his treasure in his hand he said, “Shrink, shrink, shrink,” and it became as small as an embroidery needle, tiny enough to be hidden in his ear. “Your Majesty,” the monkeys cried out in astonishment, “bring it out and play with it again.” So the Monkey King brought it out of his ear again, laid it on the palm of his hand, and said, “Grow, grow, grow.” It became as thick as a peck again and twenty feet long. Now that he was really enjoying himself he bounded over the bridge and went out of the cave. Clasping his treasure he used some of his heaven and earth magic, bowed, and shouted, “Grow.” He became a hundred thousand feet tall; his head was as big as a mountain, his waist like a range of hills, his eyes flashed like lightning, his mouth seemed to be a bowl of blood, and his teeth were as swords and halberds; the cudgel in his hands reached up to the Thirty-third Heaven and down to the Eighteenth Hell. The tigers, leopards and wolves, the beasts of the mountain, and the seventy-two monster kings all kowtowed and bowed in terror, trembling so much that they went out of their minds. A moment later he reverted to his proper size, turned his treasure into an embroidery needle, hid it in his ear, and went back to the cave. The panic-stricken kings of the monsters all came to offer their congratulations.

translation: You see this monkey king, parting the waterway, heading straight back to the Iron Plate Bridge, darting up onto it. There, the four old monkeys, leading the other monkeys, were all waiting at the bridge's edge. Suddenly, they saw Monkey King leap out of the waves, completely dry and glittering, walk across the bridge. Startled, the monkeys all kneeled down, exclaiming, "Great King, how splendid! How splendid!" Monkey King smiled with a pleasant expression, sitting majestically on his throne, his iron rod standing upright in the center. The monkeys, ignorant of his power, all tried to take the treasure, but it was as if a mosquito tried to move an iron tree—absolutely immovable. Each one bit their finger, sticking out their tongues, saying, "Grandfather! It's so heavy, how did you bring it back?" Approaching, Monkey King stretched out his hand, grabbing it and smiling at the crowd, "Every object has its owner. This treasure has been sealed in the ocean for thousands of years, and just so happened to shine this year. The dragon king thought it was just a black iron block, calling it the divine treasure at the bottom of the天河. None of them could lift it, so they asked me to fetch it. Back then, the treasure was over two丈tall, as thick as a bucket; I grabbed it, thinking it was too big, and it became much smaller; when I made it smaller, it became even smaller; again, when I made it smaller, it became even smaller. Looking back at the sky, there were characters written on it, reading '如意金箍棒, 一万三千五百斤.' Step back, let me change it again for you." He tossed the treasure in his hand, calling out, "Smaller! Smaller! Smaller!" Instantly, it shrank into a needle-like shape, small enough to be hidden in the ear. The monkeys were frightened, calling out, "Great King, take it out and show us again!" Monkey King really took it out of his ear, placing it in his palm and calling out, "Bigger! Bigger! Bigger!" It immediately grew to the thickness of a bucket, over two丈tall. He was delighted as he leaped onto the bridge, stepping outside the cave, seizing the treasure, and using his power to transform his body, stretching his waist and calling out, "Long!" He grew to be ten thousand feet tall, his head like a mountain, waist like a ridge, eyes like lightning, mouth like a blood盆, teeth like swords; in his hand, that rod reached up to the Thirty-Three Heavens and down to the Eighteen Hells, frightening all the tigers, leopards, wolves, and foxes, the mountain's monsters, the seventy-two cave kings, who all prostrated themselves, trembling with fear. Instantly, he retracted his transformation, changing the treasure back into a needle and hiding it in his ear, returning to the cave. The various cave kings were all in a panic, coming to congratulate him.

They suddenly beheld Wukong leaping out of the waves: there was not a drop of water on his body as he walked onto the bridge, all radiant and golden. The various monkeys were so astonished that they all knelt down, crying, “ Great King, what marvels! What marvels!” Beaming broadly, Wukong ascended his high throne and set up the iron rod right in the center. Not knowing any better, the monkeys all came and tried to pick the treasure up. It was rather like a dragonfly attempting to shake an ironwood tree: they could not budge it an inch! Biting their fingers and sticking out their tongues, every one of them said, “O Father, it’s so heavy! How did you ever manage to bring it here?” Wukong walked up to the rod, stretched forth his hands, and picked it up. Laughing, he said to them, “Everything has its owner. This treasure has presided in the ocean treasury for who knows how many thousands of years, and it just happened to glow recently. The Dragon King only recognized it as a piece of black iron, though it is also said to be the divine rarity which fixed the bottom of the Heavenly River. translation: — No, Constantin wasn't there then; he went on a mission... to Empress Joséphine; but instead, there were two ordinaries, a few Polish ulans... well, that was the whole entourage, except for the generals, of course, and the marshals Napoleon took with him to inspect the terrain, the positioning of the troops, and to confer... More often than not, he was accompanied by Duroc: a huge, portly, cool-headed man in glasses with a peculiar gaze. With him, the emperor usually consulted. Napoleon valued his thoughts. I remember they had been deliberating for several days; Duroc came both in the morning and in the evening, and they often argued. Finally, Napoleon seemed to be on the verge of agreement. They were in the office alone, and I, the third person, was barely noticed by them. Suddenly, Napoleon's gaze falls on me, and a strange thought crosses his eyes. "Child!" he says to me suddenly, "What do you think: if I were to adopt Orthodoxy and emancipate your slaves, would the Russians follow me?" "Never!" I exclaimed in indignation. Napoleon was struck. "In the patriotic eyes of this child," he said, "I read the opinion of the whole Russian people. Enough, Duroc! These are all fantasies! State your other plan."
source_text: — Н-нет, Констана тогда не было; он ездил тогда с письмом... к императрице Жозефине; но вместо него два ординарца, несколько польских улан... ну, вот и вся свита, кроме генералов, разумеется, и маршалов, которых Наполеон брал с собой, чтоб осматривать с ними местность, расположение войск, советоваться... Всего чаще находился при нем Даву, как теперь помню: огромный, полный, хладнокровный человек в очках, с странным взглядом. С ним чаще всего советовался император. Он ценил его мысли. Помню, они совещались уже несколько дней; Даву приходил и утром, и вечером, часто даже спорили; наконец Наполеон как бы стал соглашаться. Они были вдвоем в кабинете, я третий, почти не замеченный ими. Вдруг взгляд Наполеона случайно падает на меня, странная мысль мелькает в глазах его. «Ребенок! — говорит он мне вдруг, — как ты думаешь: если я приму православие и освобожу ваших рабов, пойдут за мной русские или нет?» — «Никогда!» — вскричал я в негодовании. Наполеон был поражен. «В заблиставших патриотизмом глазах этого ребенка, — сказал он, — я прочел мнение всего русского народа. Довольно, Даву! Всё это фантазии! Изложите ваш другой проект».
gt_translation: - N-no, Constant was not there then; he then went with a letter ... to the Empress Josephine; but instead of him, two orderlies, several Polish lancers ... well, that’s the whole retinue, except for the generals, of course, and the marshals, whom Napoleon took with him to inspect the area, the disposition of troops, consult with them ... Most often he was with him Davout, as I remember now: a huge, stout, cold-blooded man with glasses, with a strange look. The emperor consulted with him most often. He appreciated his thoughts. I remember they had been conferring for several days; Davout came both in the morning and in the evening, often even arguing; Finally, Napoleon seemed to agree. They were alone in the office, I was the third, almost unnoticed by them. Suddenly Napoleon's gaze accidentally falls on me, a strange thought flickers in his eyes. "Child! he suddenly says to me, “what do you think: if I convert to Orthodoxy and free your slaves, will the Russians follow me or not?” - "Never!" I exclaimed indignantly. Napoleon was amazed. “In the eyes of this child that shone with patriotism,” he said, “I read the opinion of the entire Russian people. Enough, Davou! All this is fantasy! Submit your other project."

human_translations.translator_1: “No, Constant was not there. He was taking a letter to… the Empress Josephine at the time. His place was taken by a couple of ordnance officers, some Polish uhlans… well, that was about it, apart from the generals, you understand, and marshals, whom Napoleon used to take with him to survey the lie of the land, the disposition of the troops, to take counsel… Of them all Davout was most frequently in attendance. I remember him well. Huge, corpulent, a dispassionate man in glasses, with hawkish eyes. The Emperor sought his counsel most of all. He had a high regard for him. I remember they held counsel for several days in a row. Davout used to come both in the morning and in the evening, often they didn’t see eye to eye with each other. In the end Napoleon would give the impression he agreed. It was just the two of them in the office, apart from me, who remained unnoticed. Suddenly, Napoleon’s eyes fell on me, a strange thought flashed in them. ‘ My child!’ he said unexpectedly. ‘What think you, if I were to embrace the Orthodox faith and free your slaves, would the Russians follow me, or not?’ – ‘Never!’ I exclaimed with indignation. Napoleon was astonished. ‘In this child’s eyes, resplendent with patriotism,’ he said, ‘I have read the mind of the whole Russian people. Enough, Davout! All this is sheer fantasy! Come to your other project.’”

Most often Davoust would be with them, as I remember now: an enormous, stout, cool-headed man in spectacles, with a strange look in his eyes. It was with him that the emperor most often took counsel. The emperor valued his thoughts. I remember that they had already spent several days in consultation; Davoust would come both in the morning and in the evening, often they even engaged in arguments; at last Napoleon seemed to begin to agree with him. Let me hear your other plan.”

Instead of him there were always a couple of orderlies—and that was all, excepting, of course, the generals and marshals whom Napoleon always took with him for the inspection of various localities, and for the sake of consultation generally. I remember there was one—Davoust—nearly always with him—a big man with spectacles. They used to argue and quarrel sometimes. translation: —"No, Constant was not there then; he went with a letter... to Empress Josephe; but instead, two orderly riders, a few Polish ulan cavalrymen... well, that was the entire entourage, of course, except for the generals and the marshals, which Napoleon always took with him to inspect the terrain, the disposition of the troops, and to consult... More often than anyone else, he was found with Duroc: a tall, bulky, composed man in glasses with an odd look in his eyes. He was the one the emperor usually consulted; Napoleon esteemed his thoughts. I remember they had been deliberating for several days; Duroc came and went in the morning and evening, and often they would even argue; finally, Napoleon seemed to be about to agree. We were in the study, and I was the third, barely noticed by them. Suddenly, Napoleon's gaze accidentally fell upon me, and a strange thought flashed in his eyes. "Boy!—he said to me suddenly—what do you think: if I were to adopt Orthodoxy and liberate your slaves, would the Russians follow me?"—"Never!"—I cried in indignation. Napoleon was struck. "In the glowing eyes of this child," he said, "I read the opinion of all of Russia. Enough, Duroc! All this is merely imagination! Outline your other proposal."
source_text: — Н-нет, Констана тогда не было; он ездил тогда с письмом... к императрице Жозефине; но вместо него два ординарца, несколько польских улан... ну, вот и вся свита, кроме генералов, разумеется, и маршалов, которых Наполеон брал с собой, чтоб осматривать с ними местность, расположение войск, советоваться... Всего чаще находился при нем Даву, как теперь помню: огромный, полный, хладнокровный человек в очках, с странным взглядом. С ним чаще всего советовался император. Он ценил его мысли. Помню, они совещались уже несколько дней; Даву приходил и утром, и вечером, часто даже спорили; наконец Наполеон как бы стал соглашаться. Они были вдвоем в кабинете, я третий, почти не замеченный ими. Вдруг взгляд Наполеона случайно падает на меня, странная мысль мелькает в глазах его. «Ребенок! — говорит он мне вдруг, — как ты думаешь: если я приму православие и освобожу ваших рабов, пойдут за мной русские или нет?» — «Никогда!» — вскричал я в негодовании. Наполеон был поражен. «В заблиставших патриотизмом глазах этого ребенка, — сказал он, — я прочел мнение всего русского народа. Довольно, Даву! Всё это фантазии! Изложите ваш другой проект».

translation: In these already dark portals, it was now very dark: a looming thundercloud had swallowed the evening light. As the prince approached the house, the cloud suddenly split open and rained down. At the same moment, when he impulsively took a step forward after a brief pause, he was at the very entrance of the gate, right under the gate leading to the street. Suddenly, he saw a person in the depths of the gate, in the half-light, at the entrance to the staircase. This person seemed to be waiting for something, but quickly flashed by and disappeared. The prince could not clearly make out this person and, of course, could not say with certainty who he was. Moreover, so many people could have passed by here; there was an inn, and people continuously moved through the corridors and back. But he suddenly felt the most complete and irresistible conviction that he recognized this person and that this person was undoubtedly Rogozhin. The prince immediately dashed up the stairs after him, his heart pounding. "Everything will be resolved now!" he muttered to himself with a strange certainty.
source_text: В этих воротах, и без того темных, в эту минуту было очень темно: надвинувшаяся грозовая туча поглотила вечерний свет, и в то самое время, как князь подходил к дому, туч» вдруг разверзлась и пролилась. В то же время, когда он порывисто двинулся с места после мгновенной остановки, он находился в самом начале ворот, у самого входа под ворота с улицы. И вдруг он увидел в глубине ворот, в полутемноте, у самого входа на лестницу, одного человека. Человек этот как будто чего-то выжидал, но быстро промелькнул и исчез. Человека этого князь не мог разглядеть ясно и, конечно, никак бы не мог сказать наверно: кто он таков? К тому же тут так много могло проходить людей; тут была гостиница, и беспрерывно проходили и пробегали в коридоры и обратно. Но он вдруг почувствовал самое полное и неотразимое убеждение, что он этого человека узнал и что этот человек непременно Рогожин. Мгновение спустя князь бросился вслед за ним на лестницу. Сердце его замерло. «Сейчас всё разрешится!» — с странным убеждением проговорил он про себя.

translation: While they were feasting, the Monkey King suddenly put down his cup and asked, "What is the rank of this 'Keeper of Horses'?" The others replied, "That is the title." The King asked, "Is this a position of what rank?" They said, "It has no rank." The King replied, "No rank? It must be a very high position." They said, "No, no, it is merely an 'ungraded' position." The King asked, "What does 'ungraded' mean?" They said, "It is the lowest rank. Such a position is the lowest and smallest, merely for looking after the horses. After Your Excellency arrived here and showed such diligence, if the horses became fat and healthy, all you would hear is a 'good' word. If they were a bit sickly, you would still be scolded; and if they were seriously harmed, you would have to pay a fine and face punishment." Hearing this, the King's anger flared up, his teeth clenched in rage. He said, "They are belittling me! In Flower Fruit Mountain, I ruled as king and lord, so what do they want me to come here to look after horses for? A horse-keeper is a lowly, menial task, not something fit for me. I won't do it! I won't do it! I'll go!" With a loud crash, he pushed the table over, pulled out his treasure from his ear, shook it to the size of a bowl, and performed his fighting skills until he burst out of the Stable Office for the Imperial Horses and straight to the South Heaven Gate. The heavenly guards knew that he was an immortal who had been enrolled as a Keeper of Horses, and dared not obstruct him, but let him go through the heaven gate.
source_text: 正在欢饮之间，猴王忽停杯问曰：“我这‘弼马温’是个甚么官衔？”众曰：“官名就是此了。”又问：“此官是个几品？”众道：“没有品从。”猴王道：“没品，想是大之极也。”众道：“不大，不大，只唤做‘未入流’。”猴王道：“怎么叫做‘未入流’？”众道：“末等。这样官儿，最低最小，只可与他看马。似堂尊到任之后，这等殷勤，喂得马肥，只落得道声‘好’字，如稍有些尪羸，还要见责；再十分伤损，还要罚赎问罪。”猴王闻此，不觉心头火起，咬牙大怒道：“这般藐视老孙！老孙在花果山，称王称祖，怎么哄我来替他养马？养马者，乃后生小辈，下贱之役，岂是待我的？不做他！不做他！我将去也！”忽喇的一声，把公案推倒，耳中取出宝贝，幌一幌，碗来粗细，一路解数，直打出御马监，径至南天门。众天丁知他受了仙录，乃是个弼马温，不敢阻当，让他打出天门去了。

translation: I am a Buddhist monk sent by the Emperor of Great Tang on a mission to the Western Heavens to worship Buddha and seek scriptures. Just now, when I arrived here, I met with some fierce wolves, tigers, serpents, and insects surrounding me, preventing me from advancing further. Suddenly, I saw Governor Hou arrive, and all the beasts fled, saving my life. Thank you! Thank you! Governor Hou said, "I live here and rely on hunting wolves and tigers for a living, and trapping serpents and insects for sustenance, which is why the beasts fear me. You being from Great Tang is like being from the same village. This place is still within the borders of Great Tang, and I am also a commoner of Great Tang. We both drink from the same land and water, and indeed we are fellow countrymen. Fear not, follow me, and rest at my dwelling. Tomorrow, I will see you off." Upon hearing this, Tang Sanzang was overjoyed and thanked Governor Hou, then followed him with the horse.
source_text: “贫僧是大唐驾下钦差往西天拜佛求经的和尚。适间来到此处，遇著些狼虎蛇虫，四边围绕，不能前进。忽见太保来，众兽皆走，救了贫僧性命，多谢！多谢！”伯钦道：“我在这里住人，专倚打些狼虎为生，捉些蛇虫过活，故此众兽怕我走了。你既是唐朝来的，与我都是乡里。此间还是大唐的地界，我也是唐朝的百姓，我和你同食皇王的水土，诚然是一国之人。你休怕，跟我来，到我舍下歇马，明朝我送你上路。”三藏闻言，满心欢喜，谢了伯钦，牵马随行。

translation: Good Monkey King, recited a spell, mounted a fierce wind, and descended from the clouds. He called out, "Children, open your eyes." The monkeys put their feet on solid ground and recognized their home, each filled with joy, rushing to the old path to the cave entrance. The monkeys inside, all gathered to greet him, then took their ranks and paid respects to the Monkey King. They arranged wine and fruits to welcome him, and asked about his battle with the demons and his rescue of his son. The Monkey King explained in detail, and the monkeys praised him endlessly, saying, "Your Majesty went to that distant place and learned such skills!" The Monkey King then said, "When I left you all, I drifted with the waves, crossing the Eastern Sea, and arrived at the South Hemisphere of Jambudvipa, learning to appear human, wearing these clothes and shoes. I roamed around for over eight years, but found no Tao. I then crossed the Western Sea and arrived at the borders of the Land of the West Ho, where I sought guidance for a long time. Happily, I met an old ancestor who taught me the true cultivation that can equal the life of heaven, the great method to achieve immortality and eternal life." The monkeys congratulated him, all saying, "It is a rare occurrence in a thousand ages!" The Monkey King then smiled and said, "Children, we are also glad that each of us has a surname now." The monkeys asked, "What is Your Majesty's surname?" The Monkey King replied, "From now on, I am known as Sun, and my Dharma name is Wukong." Upon hearing this, the monkeys clapped their hands in joy and said, "Your Majesty is Old Sun, and we are all Second Sun, Third Sun, Fine Sun, Small Sun—sons of the family, sons of the nation, and even sons of the nest!" They all came to court Old Sun, using large and small bowls, coconuts, grape wine, divine flowers, and divine fruits, truly a family celebration! Ah! The whole family rejoices as one surname unites. It remains to be seen how this story ends and how things turn out for this family in the end. Tune in for the next chapter.
source_text: 好猴王，念声咒语，驾阵狂风，云头落下。叫：“孩儿们，睁眼。”众猴脚屣实地，认得是家乡，个个欢喜，都奔洞门旧路。那在洞众猴，都一齐簇拥同入，分班齿序，礼拜猴王。安排酒果，接风贺喜，启问降魔救子之事。悟空备细言了一遍，众猴称扬不尽道：“大王去到那方，不意学得这般手段！”悟空又道：“我当年别汝等，随波逐流，飘过东洋大海，径至南赡部洲，学成人像，着此衣，穿此履，摆摆摇摇，云游八九年馀，更不曾有道；又渡西洋大海，到西牛贺洲地界，访问多时，幸遇一老祖，传了我与天同寿的真功果，不死长生的大法门。”众猴称贺。都道：“万劫难逢也！”悟空又笑道：“小的们，又喜我这一门皆有姓氏。”众猴道：“大王何姓？”悟空道：“我今姓孙，法名悟空。”众猴闻说，鼓掌忻然道：“大王是老孙，我们都是二孙、三孙、细孙、小孙、——一家孙、一国孙、一窝孙矣！”都来奉承老孙，大盆小碗的，椰子酒、葡萄酒、仙花、仙果，真个是合家欢乐！咦！贯通一姓身归本，只待荣迁仙录箓名。毕竟不知怎生结果，居此界终始如何，且听下回分解。

human_translations.translator_1: Dear Monkey King. He recited a spell, rode for a while on a fierce wind, and then lowered the direction of the cloud. “Little ones,” he cried, “open your eyes!” The monkeys felt solid ground beneath their feet and recognized their home territory. In great delight, every one of them ran back to the cave along the familiar roads and crowded in together with those waiting in the cave. They then lined up according to age and rank and paid tribute to the Monkey King. Wine and fruits were laid out for the welcome banquet. When asked how he had subdued the monster and rescued the young ones, Wukong presented a detailed rehearsal, and the monkeys broke into unending applause. “Where did you go, Great King?” they cried. “We never expected that you would acquire such skills!” “The year I left you all,” Wukong said, “I drifted with the waves across the Great Eastern Ocean and reached the West Aparagodānīya Continent. translation:
This orderly presentation initially stunned K. However, he spoke just as softly as the painter: "I believe you contradict yourself." "How so?" the painter asked patiently, leaning back with a smile. This smile made K. feel as though he was about to uncover contradictions not just in the painter’s words, but in the very court proceedings themselves. Yet, K. did not back down and said, "You once remarked that the court was inaccessible to evidence. Later, you limited this to the public court. Now, you even claim that the innocent need no help from the court. This is a contradiction. Additionally, you previously stated that one could influence the judges personally, but you now deny that genuine acquittals, as you call them, can ever be achieved through personal influence. This is the second contradiction."

"These contradictions are easily resolved," the painter said. "We are talking about two different things: what the law says and what I have personally experienced. You must not confuse them. The law, which I have admittedly never read, clearly states that the innocent are acquitted, but it does not state that the judges can be influenced. Now, I have personally experienced the opposite. I know of no genuine acquittals, but I have known many influences. It is of course possible that in all the cases I know, there was no innocence. But is that not unlikely? In so many cases, no innocence at all? As a child, I carefully listened to my father’s tales of trials at home, and even the judges who came to my studio spoke of the court. We talk about nothing else in our circles. Hardly had I the chance to sit in judgment myself that I used it, and countless trials I have heard, followed, and—admit it—I have experienced no genuine acquittals."

"None of them," K. said, as though to himself and his hopes. "This confirms my view of the court. It is also futile from this side. A single executioner could replace the entire court."

"You must not generalize," the painter said unsatisfied, "I only spoke of my experiences."

"That’s enough," K. said, "or have you heard of acquittals from earlier times?"

"Such acquittals," the painter replied, "did occur. However, it is very difficult to ascertain. Final decisions of the court are not made public and are not even accessible to the judges, so only legends have survived about old court cases. These legends do contain, in the majority, real acquittals, and you can believe them, but they are not provable. Nonetheless, one should not entirely neglect them; they certainly contain some truth, and they are very beautiful. I myself have painted several pictures based on such legends."

"Bare legends do not change my opinion," K. said, "you cannot cite them in court?"

The painter laughed. "No, you cannot," he said.

"Then it is useless to talk about it," K. said, willing to accept all of the painter’s opinions for the moment, even if he found them unlikely and they contradicted other reports. He had no time to verify or refute everything the painter said; it was already an achievement if he could persuade the painter to help in some small, non-decisive way. Therefore, he said, "Let us, therefore, set aside the genuine acquittal and you mentioned two other possibilities."

"These are the apparent acquittal and the postponement," the painter said. "These are the only ones that matter." "Before we discuss this, could you not take off your coat? It’s very hot."

"Yes," K. said, having focused solely on the painter’s explanations but now breaking out in sweat when reminded of the heat. "It’s almost unbearable."

The painter nodded as though he understood K.’s discomfort very well. "Could we not open the window?" K. asked. "No," the painter said. "It’s a fixed glass pane; you can’t open it."

K. realized he had been hoping that either the painter or he would suddenly go to the window and break it. He was prepared to inhale the fog with an open mouth. The feeling of being completely shut out of the air made him dizzy. He lightly slapped the feather bed next to him and said with a weak voice, "This is uncomfortable and unhealthy."

"Oh no," the painter said to defend his window, "the warmth is better retained here because, though it’s only a single pane, it does so better than a double window. If I want to air it, which isn’t necessary, as the gaps between the beams let in air from all sides, I can open another door or even both."

K., comforted somewhat by this explanation, looked around to find the other door. The painter noticed this and said, "It’s behind you, I had to place the bed in front of it."
